assertions.description: The handoff mechanism the demos exercise is real: HTMLAnchorElement supports the download attribute, the standard way a page asks the browser to treat a link as a file to save rather than a navigation.
The download attribute reflects as a string IDL attribute, so a page can suggest a filename — a suggestion is all it is; the browser (and from Chrome 155, a DLP rule) owns the actual destination.
A page can mint bytes and name them for download: Blob construction and URL.createObjectURL/revokeObjectURL work, which is how the demos generate real files to hand to the download pipeline.
assertions.test: (()=>{try{const b=new Blob(['x'],{type:'text/plain'});if(b.size!==1)return false;const u=URL.createObjectURL(b);const ok=typeof u==='string'&&u.startsWith('blob:');URL.revokeObjectURL(u);return ok;}catch(e){return false;}})()

assertions.description: Enforce cloud storage is enforced browser-side and exposes nothing to page script — this passes when every plausible surface for a download outcome or DLP verdict is absent: navigator.downloads, navigator.enterprise, document.downloadPolicy, and any ondownload event slot on anchors. A pass asserts the absence, which is the feature's actual web-facing contract.
assertions.test: (()=>{try{const absent=(p)=>{const parts=p.split('.');let c=globalThis;for(const part of parts){if(c==null)return true;c=c[part];}return c===undefined;};return ['navigator.downloads','navigator.enterprise','document.downloadPolicy','HTMLAnchorElement.prototype.ondownload'].every(absent);}catch(e){return false;}})()

assertions.description: The control that makes the absence assertion worth anything: the same guarded-path technique must find something that exists (navigator.permissions) and miss something that does not. Without it, a broken probe and a genuine absence produce identical results.

The enforcement itself — a triggered File-download DLP rule marking the item FORCE_SAVE_TO_GDRIVE/ONEDRIVE, skipping local storage and uploading to the corp drive — cannot be exercised from a public web page: it requires a managed Chrome 155 profile whose admin created the rule. Verifiable only by manual observation of the downloads UI and the corp drive on such a profile.
assertions.test: Requires an enterprise-managed Chrome 155 desktop profile with a File-download DLP rule whose action is Enforce cloud storage; no page-visible signal exists by design.
